patterns.title: Practice Swatch
patterns.notes: Hook 5.0 mm · Worsted (medium 4) cotton or acrylic · Finishes about 12 cm square
steps: Chain 21. That is 20 stitches wide plus one turning chain, so the swatch stays square.
Single crochet (sc) in the second chain from the hook, then in each chain across — 20 sc.
Chain 1 and turn, so the next row starts at the same height as the one below it.
Single crochet in each stitch across — 20 sc again. Repeat this row until you have 20 rows.
Lay the swatch flat and measure it. Smaller than 12 cm means try a larger hook; larger means try a smaller one.
Fasten off (FO), cut the yarn, draw the tail through the last loop, and weave both ends in.

patterns.title: Cotton Dishcloth
patterns.notes: Hook 5.0 mm · Worsted (medium 4) cotton · Finishes about 22 cm square · One evening
steps: Chain 31 loosely. Thirty stitches plus one turning chain sets the width of the cloth.
Single crochet (sc) in the second chain from the hook and in each chain across — 30 sc.
Chain 1 and turn.
Single crochet in each stitch across to the end of the row — 30 sc.
Count the stitches every few rows. Thirty every time is what keeps both side edges straight.
Repeat the turning chain and the row until the cloth is 30 rows deep, or square when you fold it corner to corner.
Fasten off (FO) and weave the ends into the back of the fabric so they cannot work loose in the wash.

patterns.title: Ridged Coaster
patterns.notes: Hook 4.0 mm · Worsted (medium 4) cotton · Finishes about 10 cm across · Worked in the round
steps: Chain 4, then slip stitch (sl st) into the first chain to close a small ring.
Chain 1, work 12 single crochet (sc) into the centre of the ring, and join with a slip stitch.
Chain 1, then work 2 sc into every stitch of the round — 24 sc — and join with a slip stitch.
Chain 1, then work one sc in the back loop only (BLO) of each stitch around. This is what raises the ridge.
Join with a slip stitch and press the coaster flat. If it cups upward, work the next round a little looser.
Fasten off (FO) and weave the tail through the back loops so the ridged edge stays even.

patterns.title: Granny Square
patterns.notes: Hook 5.0 mm · Worsted (medium 4) acrylic · Finishes about 12 cm square · Four rounds
steps: Chain 4, then slip stitch (sl st) into the first chain to make a ring.
Chain 3 — it stands in for your first double crochet (dc) — then work 2 more dc into the ring.
Work three more clusters of 3 dc into the ring with a chain-2 corner between clusters, then chain 2 and join with a slip stitch.
Round 2: slip stitch across into the nearest corner space, chain 3, work 2 dc there, then chain 2 and work 3 dc into that same space.
Work 3 dc, chain 2, 3 dc into each of the other three corner spaces and 3 dc into each side space, then join with a slip stitch.
Work rounds 3 and 4 the same way, adding one more group of 3 dc along each side as the square grows.
Fasten off (FO), weave the ends in, and pat the square into shape with damp hands.

patterns.title: Ribbed Headband
patterns.notes: Hook 5.0 mm · Worsted (medium 4) wool or acrylic · Finishes about 5 cm wide and stretchy
steps: Chain 11. Ten stitches plus one turning chain makes a band about 5 cm wide.
Single crochet (sc) in the second chain from the hook and in each chain across — 10 sc.
Chain 1, turn, and single crochet in the back loop only (BLO) of each stitch across. This is the ribbing row.
Repeat the ribbing row until the band reaches around the head with a little stretch left, usually 50 to 55 cm.
Hold the two short ends together with the ridges lined up and slip stitch (sl st) them closed through both layers.
Fasten off (FO) and weave the ends along the seam so it lies flat against the head.

patterns.title: Simple Scarf
patterns.notes: Hook 6.0 mm · Bulky (chunky 5) yarn · Finishes about 20 cm by 150 cm · One repeated row
steps: Chain 25. Twenty-four stitches plus one turning chain gives a scarf about 20 cm wide.
Half double crochet (hdc) in the third chain from the hook and in each chain across — 24 hdc.
Chain 2 and turn.
Half double crochet in each stitch across, working the last one into the top of the turning chain — 24 hdc.
Repeat the turning chain and the row until the scarf measures about 150 cm, or as long as you would like it.
Fasten off (FO) and weave the ends back into the tips of the scarf, where they will not show.
